parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime presents universal-exposure measures, not scattered incidents: every trans visitor crosses a border apparatus directed to treat sex as fixed at birth, with a fraud cable authorising refusal and possible lifetime ineligibility on suspected misrepresentation, and documented cases of passports confiscated and travellers stranded. Facility exclusion by birth sex is enforced in a growing number of states, one documented arrest and 24-hour men's-ward holding, and custody practice (state and national) is a documented harm site — sexual assault dismissed as de minimis, no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage. Marital/partner recognition and national housing/employment recourse are real but do not touch entry screening, facilities or custody. Severity is major, not catastrophic: no execution, imprisonment not typical for visitors; outcomes are refusal, humiliation, detention, care denial. State-specific hostile layer (hostile executive order, under-19 care ban, custody record) sits atop the national regime, keeping the visitor's floor low. This exceeds anchor 0.45-B's severity (care denial) but falls below anchor 0.35-A's total exclusion without remedy, since working remedies exist in parts of the regime.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy: sex fixed at birth on passports/visas, X markers ended; case-note tag for trans visa applicants; cable directs refusal and possible permanent fraud finding on suspected misrepresentation; passports confiscated/travellers stranded; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Lawsuit against the foreign ministry pending; X passports valid until expiry; limited waiver of fraud finding exists but never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening interacts with the fraud ground — a document discrepancy can escalate to lifetime ineligibility without any state-level involvement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: state prisoner housed by birth sex, celled with sex offender who assaulted her; claims dismissed as de minimis. National corrections mandates conversion-style treatment; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse. State detention lacks gender-identity hate-crime coverage.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity (2009); housing complaints accepted by state commission under national ruling.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest in the state places a trans visitor into the documented birth-sex custody regime with judicially endorsed placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National funding bar on congruent single-sex facilities; ~19 states with government-building bans, some criminal triggers; first documented arrest in a women's restroom with 24 hours held in men's ward. State executive order endorses birth-sex segregation in bathrooms and changing rooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Most mapped states (29 + units + capital district) have no ban; the state's own statute's trigger requires refusal to depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access depends on which state the visitor is in; the state layer adds hostility without its own enforcement provision.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for anyone under 19, upheld 6-1 by state supreme court; visitor under 19 or accompanying a minor cannot obtain care. National insurance-reimbursement bar proposed for under-18 care; hospital-record subpoenas documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitor care in the state beyond ordinary national services.
care_services.interaction: A travelling parent or guardian with a trans minor faces complete care denial in the state; the minor's care could become an investigation subject under the national schools order.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; conversion-style prison policies; 'gender ideology' purges.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders enjoined or in litigation; the counterterrorism text states powers are not used against mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing (women's bill of rights, athletics ban) aligns with national framing, normalising scrutiny at every institutional touchpoint.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care banned outright statewide and upheld; national order targets teachers facilitating transition; subpoenas for minors' hospital records; sports ban passed with ten athletes affected.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor cannot obtain care for the child; the child's presentation could expose teachers or guardians to investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state/province trans-violence statistics recorded; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity; first known bathroom-law arrest involved handcuffing.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; state commission investigates housing bias claims under national housing law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to bias incidents rests on national law where state law is silent; enforcement against a trespass trigger is discretionary.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Post-2023 state marker practice beyond statutory surgery requirements unresolved; which national measures remain operative at any travel date is uncertain due to injunctions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; ongoing litigation over passport markers and executive orders; one city has private-sector protections since 2012.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation outcomes could materially raise or lower the operative regime between dossier date and travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe than 0.35-A: visitors are not systematically excluded at the border by an unpublished register with no remedy; passports issue in M/F and X passports remain valid, litigation is live, and only specific categories (athletes) face outright refusal. But the shared feature is universal, discretionary document screening.

Similar tier: care denial to minors and facility exclusion as the operative exposures, custody harm documented, remedies partial. The national fraud-cable exposure and immigration-custody abuse record push this dossier slightly above 0.45-B's severity.

Comparable to 0.55-C's ward-by-marker placement: facilities and care friction without criminal prosecution as the norm, and working recourse in some channels. This jurisdiction is more severe because entry documents carry a lifetime-fraud possibility and state custody practice is judicially endorsed.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is the national hostile framework stacked with a state hostile layer. Universal exposures dominate: every visitor's documents are screened under a birth-sex rule with a fraud lever, facility access is barred in many states and endorsed by the state's own order, and custody practice is birth-sex with documented assault and judicial dismissal. The state adds the under-19 care ban and athletics ban, making a travelling family's exposure complete within the state. Against these, marriage/partner recognition, national hate-crime and housing recourse, live litigation and, in one city, private-sector protections provide partial remedies that do not reach the border desk, the restroom or the cell. Severity is major (detention, denial, humiliation, lifetime ineligibility), not catastrophic — no execution or custodial death is documented. That combination places the jurisdiction in the elevated-risk band, near 0.52.
